records.title: Bitquery — Binance 29–30 October 2026 on-chain investigation
records.note: Bitquery reports 17 Binance-labelled hot wallets drained across nine chains between 2026-10-29 20:04 and 23:56 UTC. It says each drained wallet carries a Binance proof-of-reserves label in its address data. The XRP Ledger leg involved five accounts and approximately 233.5M XRP sent to rK21t6nGLy4MNDqhvy3pGwcLFy25qgfzMx. At the 2026-10-30 06:43 UTC balance cutoff, approximately 233.5M XRP remained at the receiver with no outgoing transaction observed. Bitquery says the XRP and Solana receiver clusters share no address with the other chains; their association with the wider incident is based on timing, unusual transaction construction and Binance's aggregate damage figure. Its transfer histories were read through approximately 02:40 UTC on non-Ethereum chains, with later receiver balances checked at 06:43 UTC. Provider address labels are not a direct byte-for-byte match to Binance's official downloadable October 1 PoR address file.

records.title: Reuters — Gone in 20 minutes: how the Binance theft unfolded
records.note: Reuters reports Binance initially suspected a compromised engineer laptop but later said its investigation had found additional breach points. Reuters attributes to TRM Labs the assessment that attackers compromised Binance's transaction-signing infrastructure, which authorized withdrawal instructions. Binance had not identified the attackers in the report and said it had no evidence of wallet private-key leakage. The precise initial access, authorization chain and root cause remained unresolved.

records.title: Reuters — Binance sets aside over $6.34 billion to cover attack losses
records.note: Reuters reports Binance said it reserved more than USD 6.34B in company funds, including USD 5B already held in impacted token assets, to address the incident. Binance also said USD 3B in assets had been frozen with industry partners and that all user funds would be publicly verified through its proof-of-reserves system. These are company-reported commitments and aggregate amounts, not independently verified XRP-specific replenishment or current XRP reserve balances.

records.title: CoinDesk — Binance hack drained wallets backing customer assets, reserve data shows
records.note: CoinDesk's review of Binance's October 1 PoR data identifies Ethereum hot wallet Binance 14 among the published reserve wallets; the article reports 89,475 ETH and 1.26B USDT held there at the snapshot, among 37 assets. It estimates the 204,500 ETH stolen from Binance 14 and Binance 16 would reduce ETH backing from 100% to approximately 94% absent replenishment; USDC had 108.26% reported coverage. This article establishes an Ethereum-specific PoR crosswalk, not an official address-file match for the five XRPL source wallets and not an XRP reserve ratio.

records.title: Binance — Proof of Reserves methodology and address-download interface
records.note: Binance's official page describes PoR as custody assets intended to cover user account balances 1:1 plus reserves, explains Merkle-tree and zk-SNARK verification, and exposes a Download All Address control. The public page was inspected, but the October 1 downloadable address file was not retrieved or hashed in this run. Binance's support FAQ says monthly user-balance snapshots occur on the first day of each month at 00:00 UTC and results are released by the seventh; the November 1 snapshot therefore needs a later published-data check.

records.title: Binance News — deposits normal, withdrawals paused during security overhaul
records.note: A Binance News post marked as the verified official account says deposits are operating normally while withdrawals remain paused during a security overhaul of withdrawal services and related addresses. Binance expected withdrawals to resume within 48 hours, described multiple contributing factors and a compromised computer as a possible entry point, and promised a fuller report. This is an expected window, not confirmation that withdrawals have resumed.
